question: Should OpenClaw make `safetyDiagnostics.emit` plus manifest-declared `safetyEventTypes` a supported external plugin contract, or keep initial AI safety telemetry core-owned until a narrower plugin API is designed?
rationale: This is a new public plugin capability and authorization model, not a mechanical bug fix; repository policy requires explicit maintainer-visible direction for plugin API additions and security-adjacent contracts.

options.title: Approve a narrow plugin contract
options.body: Sponsor a documented, versioned emission API with an explicit authorization, privacy, and compatibility contract before landing the external plugin surface.

options.title: Keep the first release core-owned
options.body: Land only an approved internal/core diagnostics path and defer external plugin emission until maintainers define the stable SDK contract.

options.title: Pause the feature direction
options.body: Close or defer the implementation if durable AI safety history and its operator retention model are not currently desired in core.

recommendation.title: Keep the first release core-owned
recommendation.body: Land only an approved internal/core diagnostics path and defer external plugin emission until maintainers define the stable SDK contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history identifies skoya as the feature-series author who can provide design context; a repository maintainer must make the final product decision.
